utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Ladies and gentlemen. I can follow the proceedings in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Oric and good morning to you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours and also good morning to my learned friends of the Defence. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. I'm here together with co-counsel, Ms. Patricia Sellers, Ms. Joanne Richardson, and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I'm Vasvija Vidovic. Together with Mr. John Jones, I represent Mr. Naser Oric. We are joined by our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic, and our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts. And good morning to the colleagues from the Prosecution as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team. Any preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So we can start with the witness. I take it that you will need the whole of today?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And also part of tomorrow or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to try and finish today, Your Honour. And just one other point, Your Honour. The way we've organised our work is for the next witness as well, to be able to be completed by the end of Friday. We believe that we'll need about an hour and a half for the examination-in-chief, which would leave enough time to the Prosecution of course if they agree, and we wouldn't like the witness to have to stay the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That was supposed to be the arrangement that we would all strive for to achieve. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Of course, we will try to support it, but we don't have a statement of this witness. We really should rely on the summary and the developments on Friday in that respect, but you should be confident that we try to support the Court in that respect. We cannot give any guarantees in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I appreciate, Mr. Wubben, and I'm sure the Defence does as well. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. We just have a technical problem in that -- I at least don't have the transcript here. I wonder if someone could assist us. I think it's just my computer, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Yes, the technician is on his way or on her way.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's been solved by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell the technicians that he or she is not needed anymore. With our thanks. So I take it that even if we finish early tomorrow with this witness, you're not going to start with the next tomorrow, you'll start with the next on Friday? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We would start with that witness on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Yes, Ms. Karic, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Some of us will be speaking in English, and therefore there is a need for what we say to be translated into your own language. And in the course of the proceedings, you will be receiving, as you are now, interpretation of what we are saying in your mother tongue. If at any time you are not receiving interpretation, or if the -- there is something faulty with the reception, please draw our attention straight away because at every moment it is important that you can follow the proceedings completely. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So on behalf of Judge Brydensholt, who is at my right, and Judge Professor Eser, who is at my left, and myself, I am -- my name is Carmel Agius and I come from Malta, I should like to welcome you to this Tribunal. Very soon you are going to start giving evidence in this case which has been instituted against Naser Oric. You are a Defence witness. In other words, you have been summoned to give evidence by the Defence team. But our rules require that before you start giving evidence, you make a solemn declaration that in the course of the -- your testimony, you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. Madam Usher, who is standing next to you, is going to give you the text of the solemn declaration. Please take it in your hands, read it out loud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. Please make yourself comfortable. Since you are a Defence witness, it will be the Defence of Mr. Oric that will start with -- start questioning you. It will be Madam Vidovic who I suppose you have met already, who will be putting questions to you. Later on, either today or tomorrow, she will be -- when she is -- she has finished with her questions she will be followed by Ms. Richardson, who is the lady nearest to you on your right, and she will cross-examine you. Cross-examination is a right that the Prosecution has, just as the accused has a right to cross-examine the Prosecution witnesses. And in terms of your solemn declaration, you have a responsibility to answer all questions, in other words, both those coming from Ms. Vidovic and those coming from Ms. Richardson, truthfully, fully and to the best of your ability. So you have no right to make any discrimination between questions coming from the Defence and questions coming from the Prosecution. If at any time you need -- you're feeling tired or emotional and you need a break, please don't hesitate. Do ask us for a short break and we will give you as many breaks as you like. We will try our best to make you feel comfortable in that seat over there and to try and finish with your testimony by the end of our sitting tomorrow. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, she is in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Karic.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Karic, since we both speak the same language, I would like to ask you to listen to my question and then allow for a short break which is going to enable the interpreters to interpret your -- the question first and then give an answer. Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Karic, can you confirm your name and your surname for the sake of the transcript, your full name?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, Edina Karic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your father's name is Ahmo?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: His nickname is Ibro, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your mother is Refija and her maiden name is Mujic?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were born on the 1st of August, 1976 in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you, Mrs. Karic, you know, when you answer questions you can look at me. After your birth you lived in Lasovac which is a hamlet in the local community Sase in the municipality of Srebrenica. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You finished primary school Mihajlo Balkovic [phoen] at Sase?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have two sons: Alen who was born in 1993; and Elvis, born in 1995?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your former husband's name is Mesud Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have a brother called Adin, and your sisters are called Ahmedina, Norfija, Zemina. They are all younger than you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Karic, prior to this testimony, I had suggested to you that you could benefit from certain protective measures; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I had also suggested for certain parts of your testimony to be provided in private session.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you did not wish to do so.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that you had nothing to be ashamed of in the course of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me clarify the reasons why the witness wishes for everything to be said in the public session. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She -- is that necessary, Ms. Vidovic? The position, as you know it, as we all know it, if at any time she wants to go into private session, we rarely say no. We very rarely say no. That's number one. So the offer is there. If she doesn't ask for private session, I mean, we continue in public session. So --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. You will have the opportunity to assess why I've said what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask the usher to show the witness a map, a map of the area of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We may also decide on our own steam to go into private session, if we consider that it is in the best interest of the witness to do so, even if the witness doesn't ask for it. So I'm making that very clear, and I am sure that you as an experienced judge and lawyer will understand. So ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you get the map, Witness?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: May I ask you now to show and mark on the map your own village, the village of Lasovac?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you just mark Lasovac and circle it? Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like you to mark the following villages: Sase, Odloznik -- Podloznik, sorry, Irici [phoen], Biljaca, Prisoj, Zaluzje, and Voljavica. These villages that you have just indicated, were those Serb or Muslim villages before the war?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Before the war, those were Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what you knew that those were Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I knew it because my parents told me about it, and I knew it because of the clothes people used to wear, and I also had relatives in those villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now indicate Gradina to us?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what was at Gradina before the war?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: The headquarters of the Sase mine was situated in Gradina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I know it because my father used to work in the mine and he worked at Gradina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what was the ethnic makeup of the population around Gradina and around the mine?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It was Muslim except for one family that was called Tubic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So that family was the only Serb family, Tubic?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: May I ask you to indicate the village of Azlica to the Trial Chamber? Then Zalazje, Obadi, Kostanovice, Neskovici, Pobrdje, and Rakovac? And now, Ms. Karic, are these Serb or Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: These are Serb villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now please indicate Bjelovac and Sikiric?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the ethnic makeup of that population before the war?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: There was mixed population there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As to Lasovac itself, I mean your village, you said it was a Muslim village. How many houses were there in your village before the war?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: About 30.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what was the Serb village bordering on your village?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: The Serb village bordering on my village was Kostanovice or rather the hamlet called Jaruge.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate Jaruge on the map and mark it on the map?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I'm informed, the hamlet of Jaruge is not marked on the map, but could you please mark the place where you believe that hamlet is by a J?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell the Trial Chamber where exactly your house was situated within your village, the village of Lasovac, that is?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Our house in the village of Lasovac was at the very beginning of the village; in other words, right across the road from the hamlet called Jaruge.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How far were the closest houses from the Serb hamlet of Jaruge from your own house?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: About a hundred metres as the crow flies or maybe 200 metres, if you walk down the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you remember who those houses belonged to, what Serbs they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. They belonged to Bosko Rankic, his sons Petko Rankic, called Pero, and his other son called Bato Rankic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether in the vicinity of the house that belonged to the Rankic family, there was another house belonging to another Serb family that you knew?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. Not too far away there was a house owned by Novak Stjepanovic called Krke.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who he used to live with in that house?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. He lived with his father Zivko and his brothers, Ilija, Ivan and Ljubo, and his sister called Janja.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How far was that house from your own?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It was about 200 metres away as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know any other people from Jaruge?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I knew all of them. There were the following families there, another Rankic family apart from the ones I've already mentioned, as well as the family called Stjepanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how far is Kostanovice from your own house?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: About a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know any people from Kostanovice, any Serbs from Kostanovice, I mean?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, I knew them all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber what a colony is?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Or, rather, Sase was divided into two parts, the upper Kolonija and the lower Kolonija, which means that the lower Kolonija was basically lower Sase.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you show to the Trial Chamber on the map, please, what was the part of Sase that you used to call lower Kolonija and what it actually is?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: On the map, the part we called Donja Kolonija, lower Kolonija, is starting from the primary school all the way to the house that belonged to the Rankic family. On both right and left, those houses were called Donja Kolonija.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mean on the right and the left side of the road? Have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, could you mark DK on the map, this part that you've just marked?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Karic, how far was Donja Kolonija from your own house?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: About 70 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know anyone from Donja Kolonija?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I knew everyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the Serb families who used to live in Donja Kolonija?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you give us the names of those families, if you can remember them?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: They are called Djokanovic, Milovanovic, Petrovic, Savinovic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber who lived in upper Sase, Gornje Sase?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Muslims. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you attended school in Sase. Did Serb children attend the same school before the war?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of 1991, did those children talk about the war?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They said that their relatives were going to war in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, you attended the eighth year of primary school according to the former Yugoslav system, you were 15 years old. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the other children who talked about these things were also 15 years old?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, that is in the course of 1991, did you see any people wearing uniforms in those Serb villages that we had mentioned earlier on?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a second. Can you tell me whether you remember any of those uniformed men? Did you know any of those people?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember, Novak Stjepanovic, nicknamed Krke, Dragan Petrovic, Krke's brother, Ivan and Ljuba. They were from Jaruge. And as to Donja Kolonija, I remember Zvonko Djokanovic, Sasa Cvetkovic, and Zeljko Djokanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How old were they at the time; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: They were young. None of them was older than 25, apart from Novak Stjepanovic, who was around 28 at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you remember, was there anything happening at the beginning of 1992 that worried your parents?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Right at the beginning of 1992, Serb women and children left their houses en masse, leaving to an unknown place for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: During April 1992, did you notice anything specific in your village, in your environs?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: At the very beginning of April, I noticed that Serbs were setting up a block near our house, a block on the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How far was the ramp on the road from your parents' house?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: About 70 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Next to the ramp, did they set up anything else?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. On the left, they put some sandbags and created a shelter for themselves, and on the other side of the ramp, they brought some sort of a container.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: During April 1992, could you personally see people moving around or at the ramp?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who they were?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Pero Rankic, Bato Rankic, Novak Stjepanovic, called Krke, and his brothers, Ilija, Ivan and Ljubo. Dragan Petrovic, Djokanovic from Donja Kolonija, Cvetkovic and Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any other people that you didn't know?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, many other people that I didn't know at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The people you mentioned, the -- did they used to spend sometime around the ramp? What were they doing there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: They wouldn't stay for too long. They would assemble there and then they would leave together.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice if someone stood guard at the ramp?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were the elderly guarding the ramp usually.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The people that you mentioned who assembled at the ramp, were they Serbs?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In April of 1992, the people that you saw assembling at the ramp, what were they wearing when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Some of them wore uniforms of the former JNA and some had camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, since you were 15, did you know what the former JNA uniforms looked like?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: We knew because during peacetime, many young boys went to serve their military service with the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say camouflage uniform, what does it look like?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It is grey, brown and green.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mean multi-coloured?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a person, by the name of Novak Stjepanovic, aka Krke. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What sort of uniform was he wearing at the time, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. On occasion he would wear a black one and sometimes he was wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could he often be seen standing at the ramp?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No. He usually just passed by, and when they were about to assemble there he was always at the ramp.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The people you mentioned that you saw them in April of 1992, were they armed, these Serbs?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were all armed. They had rifles and grenades. Some also had long, large knives.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You meant they wore them?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did your father have anything to say? Did he have any comments about those weapons, about the rifles?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. He said that these were automatic rifles and semi-automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from the people at the ramp, who you mentioned you saw in April of 1992, did you see any other people in your environment, armed people?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the ramp, I saw people assembling as well as at certain locations near their houses, and they would then go across meadows towards the villages of Andrici, Obadi and Jarlica [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember when was it that you saw that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: After mid-April, or beginning -- no, mid-April, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Those other people that you saw were armed, what did they wear?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: They were also uniformed, and they had some uniforms of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me how far Obadi is from your house? I think you said that already.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Obadi is about one kilometre away as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any movement between your village and Obadi?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw a line of armed and uniformed Serbs leaving towards those villages across meadows.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "I saw that," where did you see that from? Where were you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I could see that clearly from my own house, through my window.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You and your parents, in April of 1992, so we are talking about April of 1992, did you hear of any events in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We heard it on the news, on television, that some Arkan and Seselj's men attacked Bijeljina and Zvornik and that they were slaughtering people and imprisoning Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you misunderstood me. But apart from that, the things you heard about Bijeljina and Zvornik, did you hear of anything specific, either you or your parents, relating to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you hear it from?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: From my relative, Mujic Raja [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This relative of yours, did she come to your house, to your village, and then told you that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: She happened to have been in Ljubovija in the hospital there. She spent sometime in Bratunac and managed to break through to our villages together with a lot of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then she told you something?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. She told us that in Bratunac Muslims are being killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did she say who was killing them?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. She said that Arkan's and Seselj's men were doing that. As well as Novak Stjepanovic, aka Krke, who she knew very well, as well as other Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did she mention some locations, specifically, where that took place?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. She mentioned the school of Vuk Karadzic as well as the stadium in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When she mentioned Stjepanovic, Krke, what did she say? Where did she receive that information and how she came to know about the events at the school?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: When she was fleeing from Bratunac, she joined a group of Muslims. They had previously been released from Vuk Karadzic school.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher kindly put a document, rather an exhibit, before the witness? It is an excerpt from a book called, "Satan's Sons," written by Sejo Omeragic. Your Honours, this man is not a historian.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On page 167, I wanted to read out a paragraph. Witness, could you please direct your attention to page 167? Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Novak Stjepanovic, aka Krke, came into the hall-camp, wearing a solemn black miner's suit, splashed with blood. He leisurely carried a wooden hammer with blood dripping from it. Pero Rankic from Kostanovac was with him: 'Is there anyone from Prisoj and Biljaca?' Stjepanovic asked. There was nobody and they immediately left. It seemed to all ... detainees that they had discovered a part of the secret from the hangar. Novak Stjepanovic, Krke, could be the beast who killed people with a hammer and threw them into a canal filled with oil." Ms. Karic, that passage that I've read out to you, does that tally with what you were told by your relative as she heard that from other people who were fleeing from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this exhibit be assigned -- could this document be assigned an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's -- what's the next number, Madam Registrar, please? D75 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D750, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. So this exhibit, which is in B/C/S language consists of four pages, and in the English language also has four pages, is being tendered, received and marked as Defence Exhibit D750. Does the witness know Sejo Omeragic, by any chance? Does the witness know this person?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can ask her. I mean, it will comfort us to know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you know the person who wrote this book, the author, Mr. Sejo Omeragic?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please direct your attention again at the map that you have in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Incidentally, Ms. Vidovic, we haven't given this map an exhibit number as yet. I suggest that we do so. It should have been given 750 actually. Can we remedy that, Madam Registrar? Can we give the map 750 and the last document 751 instead? We can still do that? So the map will be 750, D750.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, since I will be using this map again. I didn't ask for the number yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the extract from Sejo Omeragic's book, "Satanski Sinovi" will be given Defence Exhibit number D751. I trust that both parties have entered the correction in their data bank. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on this map I hope you have it still in front of you, could you show us the road between Bjelovac towards Srebrenica, and tell us what locations it passes by?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The road between Bjelovac and Srebrenica --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you go -- could you start with Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Bjelovac, Prisoj, Biljaca, Neskovici, Kostanovice, Donja Kolonija, to Pod Gradina and it forks there. One road takes towards Gornje Sase, the other one towards the village of Zaluzje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The road that continues towards Zaluzje, do you know if it eventually comes to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The road that you've shown us, does it pass close to your house?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How far from your house?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Around 70 metres as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How is it situated in relation to your house?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I can see it from my house. So from Pero Rankic's house, all the way up to school, that's the part that was visible from my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I wanted to know is whether the road passes below or above your house.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Above.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what was the portion of the road that you could see?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: About one kilometre of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you remember, did you see anything taking place on that road in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw a line of cars.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When was it?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: In the second half of April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see whether anything was ahead or in front of that column?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. A police car was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it a military column or were those civilian cars?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Those were civilian vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any moment see the people who were travelling in those vehicles?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you see them?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Because they stopped at the ramp that I mentioned previously, and they assembled there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Assemble or grouped, but I wanted to ask you the following: Did they contact with anyone from the village that was next to the ramp?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. They had contact with the Serbs from Jaruge and Donja Kolonija.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of those people?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Novak Stjepanovic, aka Krke, Pero Rankic, Bato Rankic, Dragan Veselinovic, Mijo Cvetkovic, his full name is Miodrag, Sasa Cvetkovic, Zeljko -- Slobodan Djokanovic, his son Zeljko, Zvonko Djokanovic, his brothers Tomo --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned Pero Rankic. Is that the same person that was mentioned in the book, the Satan's Sons, that -- as someone who accompanied Stjepan Kerkanovic [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: He is the same person.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the area of Kostanovice, is there another Pero Rankic?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the column. You said it stopped. What happened afterwards?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Our Serb neighbours joined them, the people that I mentioned, and they left in the direction towards the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about that particular column. Did you see it again at any time?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. It returned on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How much time elapsed?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Five to six hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it the same column or did it appear to look differently?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It was much longer on its return.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you describe what it consisted of now?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: There were lots of trucks that were loaded with furniture, appliances, cattle, and luxurious vehicles were also to be seen in the column.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was your mother's reaction? Did she see the come column?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, we all saw it. She got scared and she said that they must have robbed Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The people in the column, how did they behave?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: They were drunk, disorderly, they were shooting, and singing some Chetnik songs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the column simply pass through your village as well as the neighbouring village of Jaruge or did they stay there for a while?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No. One column continued to Bjelovac. The other one went to the hamlet of Jaruge.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember exactly what vehicles came there and did you see perhaps what was the load on those vehicles?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: To Jaruge, there came one truck with cattle, furniture, appliances, as well as a number of luxurious vehicles that accompanied the truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if that part of the column went towards certain houses or in some other direction?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. It went towards the house of Novak Stjepanovic and the Rankic family who lived there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The event you described with the column, did it happen on only one occasion or on several?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It occurred on several occasions, until the 10th of May of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you observed the column, could you notice something specific or peculiar about it on their departure and on their return?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I noticed the police car that was ahead of the column, and when they came back, its lights were on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to the event you described, did you and your family know what was happening with the Muslims in your wider area?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: A lot of Muslims came to our village. They were frightened, fleeing from surrounding Muslim villages because they said they were being encircled by the Serbs and that they were killing them or taking people away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't see that, did you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about that from someone?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We heard that from many Muslims who came to our houses and to our village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember anyone in particular who came to your village or to your house and told you about those events?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember Izet Latifovic who happened to be in the village of Biljaca at the time. He suffered a shock because the village was encircled by the Serbs and they invited the Muslims to surrender. They took away many Muslims and he saw a murder take place. He fainted and that's how he survived. He came to several hours later and managed to come to our village. During that time, his father thought him dead, and committed suicide. He poisoned himself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Latifovic tell you that personally in your house?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: He said that to my parents but I was close and I could overhear.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: If I may, I hate to interrupt but could we perhaps have a date? Are we talking about May of 1992 at this point? If Madam Vidovic could just inquire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic, I was going to raise the same issue myself basically so if you could address it, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were describing something that took place in the second half of April of 1992, I believe, and then I asked you did you at that time have any knowledge about somethings that were happening. Perhaps you could tell the Chamber when was it that Mr. Latifovic came to your house?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It was around mid-May.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So in the first half of May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher now please show to the witness an excerpt from the book that was marked as D751? We have another portion. And we provided it with the bundle. It is another passage from the book called, "Satan's Sons" written by Sejo Omeragic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Karic, I wanted to read out a small portion from the book. Please take a look at that passage.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my colleague has just drawn my attention to something, to a part of the transcript that may be unclear, and perhaps I could clarify with the witness before we start reading the next excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, when you mentioned the gentleman a minute ago who came to your house, you said he fainted and that that was how he survived. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: He fled into the woods, and he saw a murder or murders take place in Biljaca and when the Serbs were inviting Muslims to surrender by megaphone, and he saw Serbs surround the village and torch it, he fainted, so they simply passed him by. They thought he was dead. When he came to, he was frightened but managed to reach our village.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for the clarification. Now I want to read the passage: On May 13, about 1.000 arrested men and women from Podsoj were beaten and pushed towards the town. The last Muslim villages around Bratunac will be destroyed by Serb neighbours. They called people by megaphone in Bojici, Biljaca, Prisoj, Zaluzje and Bjelovac, to gather ... at Srbo Jokic's house in Podbradze and to bring their ... documents with them. People abandoned their houses, and plunderers burnt them down and came right after them. The following people plundered and burnt down houses: Ratko Simic from Kunjerac, Nedjo and Pedja Rakic, Zvonko and Zeljko Djokanovic, and Dragan Jovanovic, aka Tanto. Concerning this I wanted to ask you the following. I believe you mentioned Zvonko and Zeljko Djokanovic on two occasions already. Did you see them in the column that you saw leaving and coming back?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This description of events here which includes the events at Biljaca, is this in line with what Mr. Latifovic told you about?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, did you find out about any of your relations having been killed in the beginning of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I found out that my cousin, Kiram Mujic, had been killed. His body was found by the River Drina in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you how long you stayed in your own village. Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We stayed up until the 16th or the 17th of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from these events that you've described to us, in the course of May 1992, and what I mean is the period up until the 16th or the 17th, that is to say before you left, did anything happen in the course of that period of time that gave the Muslims from Lasovac cause for concern?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was it?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Serbs were shooting from their villages, and from the ramp I mentioned earlier on there was a shooting on a daily basis, and it would frighten us and we would take to the nearest woods, and hide in the woods until the shooting stops, and then when it finally stopped we would go back home.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did anything happen that induced you to leave your houses?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. One night, after midnight, we are talking about the 16th or the 17th of May 1992 here, at some point just after midnight, there was a great deal of shooting, and I was terribly frightened and that was the first shock of that sort that I experienced in my whole life, and we were terribly scared. My sisters and my brother were scared as well. And then the shooting would stop briefly and then resume again in the early morning hours, but then shells started landing on our village as well, and a shell landed very close to our house, and the whole house shook, and the window panes were broken.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did your parents decide?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: We were all in a state of shock. We were terribly frightened and my parents decided that we had to leave the house and that we had to take to the woods.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember where you went to?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: We went in the direction of a wood above the village Lasovac in the direction of Bare.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see anyone else on your way? Were you the only ones fleeing?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No. We were certainly not the only ones. We came across quite a few Muslims in the woods, and they were all just as frightened as we were. There were people who were sick, there were screaming children, and it was terrible. People were screaming and wailing and everybody was distressed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of that flight, could you move freely or were there any combat activities?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: As we were moving through the woods in the direction of that hill, well, they were shelling all the time and a shell actually landed pretty close to us, and my youngest sister had a huge shock and she was actually unable to speak for several days.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And finally, did you find some accommodation?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We got to Bare. This was deep in the forest. It was out in the open. And when we got there, there were thousands of Muslim refugees in the area, and children were crying and people had nothing to eat, in fact, and we slept outdoors and we made tents and sheds using plastic bags or branches, and it was raining. And it was really horrific.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did the people live? What did they eat? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Sometimes people went without food for several days, or else they would pick mushrooms or leaves.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did you at any point decide to go back to your own home?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. One day after about 10 to 11 days that we spent in the forest, we had no food left and we decided to go home to get some food, and to get our cattle.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember what happened next?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: As we set out and we were on our way back to our home, we were surrounded by three soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: They were wearing uniforms and they were armed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know any of those people, any of those people who captured you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber who they were?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: They were Petar Rankic, called Pero, Stanislav Milovanovic, called Cane, and Dragan Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have I understood you correctly, Rankic Petko or Rankic Petar?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Petko Rankic called Pero.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: We were taken to Sase mine at Gradina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, now I'd like the usher to show the witness a Defence document, D92. It's a document coming from the command of the Bratunac Brigade of the 4th Battalion and it is entitled, "The list of conscripts of the battalion for December 1992."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to page 3. It's number 01320785. Or, rather, 84. So actually it's page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honours. My pages are mixed up in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you take a look at page 4. And it's actually 785; those are the three last digits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's the next one, please, it's the next one, in the English language. But I don't think we need to see the English text because I suppose what we are interested in or what we should be interested in is the list itself. So if you can just leave it in the hands of the witness and then we'll -- we can follow in a different manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you take a look at the name, number 79, Stanislav Milovanovic, son of Radoje; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then number 100.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Petko Rankic, son of Bosko. And now 102, Dragan Petrovic, son of Tatomir. Do you know these people?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. They are the people who captured us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did these people take you to the mine at Sase?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. They took us to the administrative building of the mine of the Sase mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could we just clarify this a little bit? Who else was there? Who was captured apart from you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I was with my father and my aunt, Begajeta Mujic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask the witness to stick to this document because we will be using it later on as well. So on your way to Sase mine, did you see anything else?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In Donja Kolonija, I saw that my neighbour Idriz's house was on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was your neighbour Idriz a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were brought to the Sase mine, what did you see there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I saw very many soldiers there, uniformed and armed soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How many, roughly speaking?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: About a hundred.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask the usher to show the witness another Defence Exhibit; it is document D327. It comes from the command of the Bratunac Brigade and military police dated the 24th of February, 1993, entitled, "Report on the number of men of the military police force and the pertinent particulars of the members." Witness, I'd like you to take a look at pages 2 and 3. And can you focus on the names that I'm going to point out to you?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is page 1 in the English translation, the first bit that I'm going to be reading out now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the first name I want you to focus on is Radivoje, son of Zivan, Djokanovic, born on the 20th of May, 1961, mobilised with reserve police force of Srebrenica on the 14th of April, 1992. Did police work in the territory of the Sase mine. Now, we've got the second person, the second name, on this list, Lazo Loncarevic, son of Radovan, born on the 27th of December, 1958. He and his family moved from Vitez to Doboj where he was mobilised to the front around Vukovar. On arrival in Bratunac with a group of refugees from Zenica, he was assigned to the military police squad at the Sase mine. Now, a little bit further down, the third name, from below, Milomir Veselinovic, son of Vlado, born on the 12th of April, 1949. Mobilised at reserve police in Srebrenica on the 14th of April, 1992, and discharged routine duties in the territory of the Sase mine. Now we've got the next page. The second name, Miodrag Cvetkovic, son of Milan, born on the 1st of March, 1950. Mobilised on the 19th of April, 1992 to the reserve police force in Srebrenica, where he discharged duties in the area of the Sase mine. Now, witness, can you tell us if you know any of the people whose names I've read out to you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know Radivoje Djokanovic and Miodrag Cvetkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us where they were from?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: They were from Donja Kolonija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do I take it that she doesn't know the third person or I think -- because you mentioned three names. So you could put the question yourself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Witness. You told us that you knew two of these people, Djokanovic and Cvetkovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the other two?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Can you tell us whether you remember any event having to do with Miodrag Cvetkovic in relation to the place where you were taken, the Sase mine, that is?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I remember an event, he caught two children, Fahrudin Huremovic's children, and they were captured two days before we were captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you find that out?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: When we came to the hall where we were imprisoned, those children told us about it because he was their next-door neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that day when you got there and you found about a hundred people there, did you see any of them?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who did you see?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I saw them, I saw Djokanovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm only asking about these two people who we've just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw both of them, Radivoje Djokanovic and Miodrag Cvetkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As to these hundred soldiers that you described having seen, what sort of uniforms did they have and do you remember if they had uniforms?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember they all had uniforms. They had camouflage uniforms and the older ones had the former JNA uniforms. In other words, all younger soldiers were wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd like the witness to be shown Defence Exhibit D97, which is a video document. I think it is -- it has already been prepared so we can view it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the scene on the video?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this Defence Exhibit D97 is a video which was recorded on the 15th of December in the area of Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like you to take a good look at this picture. These 100 soldiers approximately that you've described to us, when you saw them, were they wearing something resembling the uniforms that you can see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were wearing these uniforms, but they were wearing shirts, camouflage shirts as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Vidovic. How are we going to identify for the record this page or this photo or picture that we have? Because I don't see, except 02.31 at the bottom right-hand corner. Is that the reference? Okay. So for the record --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That's the reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness was shown for the record a part, a still, from the video mentioned by Madam Vidovic, at the position 02.31. All right?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with respect to this -- there is another question I'd like to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Take a good look at this picture. Do any people have different uniforms? Just look at the person who is in the background?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It's a different uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the olive-drab uniform?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I can't see it very clearly in this picture but it certainly resembles that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Now I'd like to go back to the events that you've described to us. When you arrived at Sase, where were you, your father and your aunt taken?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: We were taken to the administrative building of the mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any other people there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, about 30 people, about 30 captured Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where were they from; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I do. They were from the nearby village, Gradina, and then of us course from the village of Lasovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened to you when you entered the administrative building?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: We were taken for individual questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you yourself taken for questioning?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was Dragan Veselinovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who is he? Do you remember where he was from, for example?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was from Donja Kolonija. He was a neighbour of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Had you known him before the war?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. He had an older brother who was a police officer, and he had two sisters, two twin sisters.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, so far you've told us that you -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, is this person one of the -- that you referred the witness to earlier on, when you were --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it's a different one, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes. The transcript has been corrected. Yes, let's take it easy.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You've told us so far that you knew quite a few neighbours there, including Mr. Veselinovic. Can you please explain to the Trial Chamber what the mentality of that area is? How come you knew all these people?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Because we used to play together when we were children. I mean, it is not like it is in the west. We visit one another on holidays, and we all lived together in harmony, all of us together.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you, Witness, I think you still have the document, the list that we have looked at earlier on?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I do not, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: D92, D9-2. Could you just leave it with the witness until the end? Because we shall be going back to it. On page 1, where it says the list of conscripts of the 4th Battalion for the salaries in December 1992, and could you look at the name, number 2, Dragan Veselinovic, son of Slavomir, who is a deputy commander. Did you know that man?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was the person who was questioning us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How long did you spend at that mine altogether?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: About two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was actually at the mine when you were there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It was one of the worst possible camps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what can you claim that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: When we came to that hall, I saw the detainees who had been there before. They were frightened and you could see that they had been beaten because there were bruises on their bodies and faces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did any one of them tell you anything?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. They told us that a couple of days before our arrival, six people had been killed, six Muslims who had also been imprisoned there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who actually told you this?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that family called Omic, was there a Mrs. Omic who was a Croat?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need for the record to include something that the interpreters missed. Your question was who actually told you this. And she did give an answer but the interpreters didn't catch it. So I think we need to go back to that. You repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that your neighbours told you about the killings of six people. Who exactly told you that? Can you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The family called Omic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it was the Omic family. In that family, was there a Croat woman in that family?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. She was called Gordana, and she had two children.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What did the members of the Omic family tell you? Who had been killed?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Three women and three men had been killed. Rijad Salihovic's parents had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was the child present when it happened?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The child actually witnessed the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it also witnessed by anyone else?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Everybody present witnessed that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, sometimes we perhaps speak too fast. Can you just tell us, you mentioned a child who witnessed the killing of his parents. Could you repeat his name?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Rijad Salihovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did they tell you who killed them?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Novak Stjepanovic, Krke, with a group of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one moment. We've got another document in relation to this. I'd like to have shown to the witness. I'd like the usher to show the witness the document from the military post in Bratunac, the list of people who received reimbursement for business travel and payroll for July 1992. It's 0336289 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on page 1, or rather you should look on page 2, number 364, it says the reconnaissance sabotage platoon, and number is 364, Novak Stjepanovic, first class soldier. Is this the person you've been mentioning so far?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear about him having a rank of any sort? Because you said that he was in the army in Croatia. Has anyone ever mentioned anything about him holding a rank?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. When we went to school, children used to talk about him having received some kind of rank.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And another question in relation to this. Was there anyone else with the same name and surname anywhere in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, there was nobody else with the same name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would perhaps like for this document to be given an exhibit number. And perhaps this would be the right time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will become Defence Exhibit D752. And there is a correction that needs to go in the transcript, page 39, line 8, where there is the ERN number, that's mistaken. It should be 01336289. So thank you. We will have a break of 25 minutes starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I notice Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, I do have a submission to make to the Bench, and I would ask if we could go into private session at this time since I think these are -- we are approaching delicate matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go to private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Karic, we took a break as we were talking about certain murders and related that to Stjepan Novakovic called Krke. I would kindly ask the usher to put another document before the witness. It comes from the military post of Bratunac. Actually, it is a document that came from the command of the Bratunac Brigade, dated the 26th of May of 1994. Please take a look at the document. Its title is, "Opinion of the command of the Bratunac Brigade sent to the military court in Bijeljina," signed by the commander, Lieutenant Colonel Slavko Ognjenovic. The document's number is 04364593. It is a short document and I will quote it to you. "Opinion of the Bratunac Brigade command concerning the request to postpone the prison sentence pertaining to Reserve Sergeant Novak Stjepanovic. Upon receiving an invitation to serve his prison sentence, Reserve Sergeant Novak Stjepanovic asked for the opinion of the Bratunac Brigade command on this issue, and the command hereby submits it to the relevant court. The above-mentioned person was a member of various units in and outside of the Bratunac Brigade, and currently is serving as a member of the reconnaissance platoon as an offensive unit of this brigade. As such, he demonstrated good soldierly virtues, i.e. the virtues of a good fighter, who was brave and dedicated, and therefore this command's opinion is that his reasons for postponing the prison sentence should be taken into account and that he should serve his time only after the cessation of combat activities, law permitting." My question to the witness is the following: As far as you could see and as far as you know, was Krke a member of the Serb army in that area?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you got any idea as to why Stjepanovic, Novak, called Krke, was punished in this way?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Because he killed Zvonko Djokanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I heard that after the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We haven't given it a number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. If we could receive the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D753.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To go back to the events in the camp --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just for clarification, I won't go into detail concerning those events but I will only briefly mention some of them because they may relate to some other events that happened later.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were brought to the camp, was someone else brought along with you as well?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mirzet Garaljevic from Likari.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember him well? What did he look like?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: He was terrified, sad in appearance. He wore a blue sweatsuit and blue sneakers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who brought him in the camp?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was brought by Commander Miroljub Todorovic, aka Toso.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, Miroljub Todorovic. That's what the witness said, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, how do you know that this person, Miroljub Todorovic, was a commander?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: When he entered the hall, he introduced himself to me, my father and my aunt, and he said that he came from Nis, that he's a commander and that his name is Miroljub Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When he said that he was a commander, did he say commander of what?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, of the entire Sase area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This person, Miroljub Todorovic, was that a local Serb?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said he was from Nis. Could you tell the Chamber where that is?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: In Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please put another Exhibit, D316 in front of the witness? It is a record of soldier's death, the soldier being Miroljub Todorovic, son of Radivoje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please take a look at the document? It says "record of soldier's death," the name is Miroljub Todorovic, son of Radivoje, born in Nis in 1961. Is that the man you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Again, I do hate to interrupt, but it appears this document does not have a date, is that correct, on both the -- or at least the English doesn't, and I'm looking at the B/C/S. There is no date on it. I don't know if Madam Vidovic has additional information about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it a document that has been supplied by the Prosecution itself, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suppose I cannot ask for that information from --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour, thank you. And it's just an observation at this point now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It would be useful of course. I agree with you it would be useful for the purpose of whatever use we would make of this document to have more details about it, but I don't imagine --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- the case will depend on this document, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what I can offer is the correct data. This document is a part of documentation stemming from the Bratunac Brigade, and it was disclosed to us on CDs. That's what I can say on my part. In any case, perhaps we can clarify something with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This person, if one is to take a look at the information contained there, Miroljub Todorovic, did he himself tell you that he was from Nis?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
