utterances.text: Was his accent that of your region or did he use another accent?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: He spoke Ekavian.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Chamber where Ekavian is spoken?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: In Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he mention whether he was married?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he say he had a family?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. He said he had a wife and a son.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. The year of 1961, does that tally -- is that similar to the age that you remember him being at the time?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you whether he was a local Serb. You said he wasn't and that he was from Serbia. Apart from him, were there any other people from Serbia proper within the camp?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a group from Serbia, but most of the people were local Serbs. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What took place in the next few days with your father and your aunt?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. My father was sent to take a message to the woods in -- above Lasovac for the Muslims to surrender. He left and didn't return. A few days later they sent my aunt, Begajeta Mujic, to the village of Konjevic Polje with another such message. She didn't return either.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the time you were in the camp, were you and the other people there abused, mistreated?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who mistreated you? The local Serbs you mentioned or the people from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: We were mistreated by the local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: These local Serbs that mistreated you, did they wear uniforms and had weapons?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, both.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember some people, Serbs, that you saw in the camp of Gradina Sase?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember the Djokanovics, as well as the Rankovics; I've already mentioned them. I mentioned a Petrovic, as well as the Milovanovics. And I saw my teacher, Marinko Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This teacher of yours, Marinko Lackovic, what did he used to teach?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Chemistry and biology.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether he is still teaching today?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you sent to do something in the camp?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were sent to clean some hangars as well as to peel potatoes in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please go back to the document D92. I hope you still have it in front of you. Do you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please go to the second page and take a look at the name under number 43. Djokanovic, Slobodan, son of Stanoje. Do you know this man?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was in a uniform and with a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Take a look at the name under number 48, Dragoslav Milovanovic, son of Velicko. Did you see that person in Sase camp?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did. Several times. He also took my aunt to Bratunac to take that message to the Muslims in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The name under number 54, Kosta Rankic, son of Sreten. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. He also had a uniform and had a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him in the area of the camp?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please stay on this page. And take a look at the names under 54, 58, 60 and 62. You will see some women's names there: Danica Rankic, Nada Rankic, Jelena Veselinovic, and Vojka Milovanovic. Did you or did you not meet those women in the camp?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I met them in the camp and I saw them several times. They worked in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So they were cooks there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall Vojka Milovanovic?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did that woman look like?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: She had short, black hair, rough features, as well as voice, and she resembled a male.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did she see you and the other people in the camp?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If one was to say that that woman was not in the camp when you were there, that is at the end of May and the beginning of June, would that be true?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Serbs who worked at the mine at that time, apart from those that were part of the military, I have in mind the cooks, and everyone who was there, were they able to see what was happening to you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. They could see our moaning, our screams and the mistreatment as well as the wailing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please go to the next page. The number there is 01320785. Please look under number -- sorry, look at the name of Nenad Milovanovic, son of Dusan, as well as the name at the end of the page, Izet Kasupovic. Do these names mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. They manned the mortar that was located close to the administrative building.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a mortar that was in the proximity of the administrative building. Did you see it yourself?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you see it?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: We saw it through the window of the hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: These people, Nenad Milovanovic and Izet, how do you know that these are the people who were there? Did you know them from before?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I knew Nenad Milovanovic. He was also a neighbour of mine. And I didn't know Izet. He was called Izo at the time. And I realised that he had a Muslim name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So Izet is a Muslim name?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you said you saw a mortar. What were they doing with the mortar? Since you were 15 at the time, did you know what a mortar is?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I knew what a mortar is because I saw it in some books, and we were explained by the detainees that that was a mortar. We saw it go off.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To make it clear, when you say "I saw it in some books," is it true or not that in our part of the world, there used to be a class called protection and first aid but it also dealt with weapons?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. When we attended school, in the seventh or the eighth grade, a teacher explained some things about weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: To go back to what is it that you saw concerning that mortar, what were they precisely doing with it?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: They were firing shells from that mortar.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you hear it?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We heard the detonations. They shook the building and the window panes burst.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you mean to say that the detonation --

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: When it went off.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please continue. But before that, let us clarify something. You said Izet was a Muslim. Did the commander mention any Muslims within the Serb army, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. He mentioned him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Please continue with the list. Take a look at number 77. Radisav Milovanovic. Did you see him as well?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember any specific event concerning that person?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. He came to the hall once to take us to clean something and he attempted to rape me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone help you, or did the rape take place?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No. The commander, Miroljub Todorovic, was close by and he prevented that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please go on to the next page now. Please take a look at the number 109, Rankic, Dusan. Did you see him at the mine when you were there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How about an important under 110? Ilija Stjepanovic, son of Zilko?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. He is Novak Stjepanovic's brother.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 112, Maksim Rankic?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I saw him too.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Number 124, Marko Milic, son of Radovan. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see him when you were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Djokanovic, son of Sreten. Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Within the camp?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Savo Milovanovic, son of Sveto. Did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. He stood guard at the entrance when I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Cvjetko Bosnjacic, son of Djoko?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I saw him. He was guarding the cattle that was within the school compound at the playground.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Slavomir Veselinovic, son of Vladimir. Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him within the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Vojislav Djokanovic, son of Bogdan?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I saw him within the perimeter too.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Djokanovic, Petko, son of Vojislav?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I saw him as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Djokanovic, Milos, son of Vojislav?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And 137, Mile Petrovic, did you see him at the mine?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, all these people I've just asked you about, and with reference to whom you said that you did see them within the perimeter of the Sase mine at the time that you were there, I mean, had you known them well before you got to the mine?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. They were all my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It does not refer to Izo Kasupovic?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: With the exception of Izo Kasupovic. He was from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The administrative building of the Sase mine and the camp you were at in the month of June 1992, I mean, did you ever understand why the soldiers were there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Well, my impression was that their command post of the entire region of Sase was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that something that Miroljub Todorovic confirmed to you, as you said before?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask -- the question has already been answered, but I would ask that the witness not be led and that certain questions should be put to her so she can answer and not suggestions of answers so she simply responding yes. If Madam Vidovic could please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In this particular context?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, in this particular context, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic you've been put on notice by Ms. Richardson that --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I simply repeated a fact already stated by the witness herself five or ten minutes ago but I'll take account of it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a mortar. In the immediate -- did you see anything else of the sort in the immediate vicinity of the mine, other than the mortar?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw a tank right next to the building, just below the window of the hall where we were kept.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it simply parked there or what?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It left every day, and they took the tank somewhere and then they brought it back again.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How would you describe the tank?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It was an olive drab colour, camouflage paint. And there was a machine-gun on the tank, mounted on the tank. And the ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, whilst you were at the camp, of a large group of people having been brought to the camp?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when that happened?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It was in the beginning of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who brought those people in?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Commander Miroljub Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how many people were in the group?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: About 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were they men or women?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: There were men and four women. Out of those four women, one was heavily pregnant, and another woman had two children, and all the rest of them were men.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where were they from?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: They were from Suha.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if the witness still has the map, I would like her to indicate Suha on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you still have the map, Ms. Karic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So could you be kind enough to put circle around Suha, please? If you know where it is. Or if you can find it on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've just marked it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Karic, how did you know that those people were from Suha?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: When they came into our hall, we could see that they had been beaten up and they were extremely frightened and they told us that they were picked up in the woods around Suha and that some of them had been taken to Bratunac to the Vuk Karadzic school and another group was brought to us, to the same hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you whether there were any other people in the woods?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: There were large numbers of people in the woods. They saw another group before they were captured. They saw a group of people who had been killed and then a couple of days later, all of them were captured as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: These people hiding in the woods that we are referring to and the people who had been killed, were they Muslims?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you personally find out that some of those people from the woods had been taken to Bratunac? Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I've already mentioned that there was a heavily pregnant woman in the group and she was crying most of the time because her husband had been taken to the Vuk Karadzic school.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Vuk Karadzic school is in Bratunac, right?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Karic, apart from these men and women from Suha, can you tell us whether in this group of people of about 30 people who had been captured, yourself included, were there any women and children in the group who -- when you were there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how many?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: There were nine children ranging between one and a half and 12 years of age. And in the age group of 15 to 18, I mean there were girls, and there were seven or eight women who were older than 20, and all the rest of them were men.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How can you tell me that there were nine children? How do you know?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I know because I myself was there and I knew all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Do you remember what went on in the following period?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: In the following period, Commander Todorovic came to the hall with a list and he said, "Those whose names I call out will be taken for an exchange at Zvornik, and those who are not called out will stay here."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was anyone called out?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. About 51 people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was not called out; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Gordana Omic and her two children, and six girls, myself included.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any idea as to why Gordana Omic and her two children were not called out?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Because she used to work as a secretary in the administrative building before the war because they needed her to help them type documents and to help them with the secretarial work.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they take her to work; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, on a daily basis. She had to type things up for them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, on the basis of what you yourself saw, what happened to that group of people who had been called out?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. A year -- an hour later, two lorries drove up in front of the building and the commander, together with the group of soldiers, took those who had been called out outside and they were loaded onto those lorries. And there was a lot of screaming in the hall at that stage, and the children started crying and it was terrible. Words are failing me in trying to describe it but it was terrible. People were being pushed onto lorries, and one woman was unable to get on, and she was hit and then thrown on to the lorry basically.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After those events, have you ever seen any of those people alive?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No, never, not a single one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have I understood you correctly that some of your neighbours from Gradina were in that group?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were people of from Suha who had been brought in as well as all of my neighbours from the village Gradina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Has a single one of those neighbours from Gradina appeared and come back alive?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what about the people from Suha you've mentioned earlier? Have any one from Suha contacted you after all those events?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Quite a few of them contacted me and asked me if I knew what had happened to the members of their families.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'd like the witness to be shown the Defence Exhibit D703. It's a video clip of Suha.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Richardson, is this the one that --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's my understanding that it is. That this video contains images of bodies, et cetera. But I have to tell you that we were just this morning given a clear copy of the video, so perhaps Madam Vidovic can tell us what's on the video. And I renew my application, if that's the case, that it does contain bodies, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic. I trust in your judgement.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, perhaps it would Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. be a good idea to have this video shown in a private session. I'm not against it. But there is another point. This is a video that the Prosecution had received with other Defence exhibits prior to the Defence -- Pre-Defence Conference, so it was as far back as July. Quite a while back. That's what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: I apologise, Madam Vidovic. But we're not complaining. It's just that the video that we did receive hasn't worked and so we received a copy this morning that is working. And it's not a complaint on the Defence's part as all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's not make of it a casus belli. Madam Vidovic, shall we go then in private session for the purposes of relaying this video? And then when we come to questions -- unless you want to put the questions as we go along. In that case, we will remain in private session. If you want to show the video first and put the questions after, what we will do is we see the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- in private session and then you put the questions in open session. It's up to you. I mean, I wouldn't -- I wouldn't --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Precisely, Your Honour. We can first watch the video. It's not very long. And then I'm going to ask questions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if it's important for you, we will see it. Let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Karic, would you be able to comment on the video yourself?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I can say that as far as I know, nine children were taken for the exchange, the ages were between one and --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you stop for a second? Do you remember whose child it was, the youngest child, I mean?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was Salcin Omic's child.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, I interrupted you. You said ranging in ages between a year and a half and 12?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: There were quite a few women. There was a heavily pregnant woman who was about to give birth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps we shouldn't pursue this any further. Thank you to the witness. What happened to you, to the girls, after that day?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: We stayed in that hall, nine of us stayed behind. We were crying. I wanted to be exchanged, but as soon as they decided to leave us there, I knew that there was something wrong. Straight after the others were taken away, the lorries came back.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you stop for a second? How long afterwards did they come back?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: After about half an hour they came back empty.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you and the other girls have any idea at the time where Zvornik was?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you comment on the fact, as to whether they had been taken to Zvornik or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We knew that Zvornik was about 50 kilometres away from Sase and there was no way they could have reached Zvornik within such a short period of time. We commented that they must have been taken somewhere in the vicinity of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember what happened to you and the other girls after that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Straight after the lorries came back, Commander Todorovic and two soldiers came into the hall and he asked for three girls, for three volunteers, to do some cleaning work in Bratunac. But none of us came forward. And then he said to the soldier who was standing next to him to choose the ones he wanted to take. He said, You, you and you. He pointed his finger at some of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the proofing for this testimony, I understood you to say that you did not want to mention the names of those girls.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you think this is relevant we can go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's put it like this: If you don't put the question, we are not going to intervene. But it doesn't mean that the Prosecution later on cannot put the question themselves upon cross-examination. So I have no right actually at this moment to ask the Prosecution what they are going to do during the cross-examination. So what I would suggest is that, unless Ms. Richardson stands up and gives us an indication, that you proceed without asking for the names and then we see if the names are asked for later on. And we will deal with it when it is necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: We were put in a car, the three of us, that is, and we were taken in the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you were leaving in the direction of Bratunac, did you drive through the area where your house was?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We drove through Donja Kolonija and I could see that my parents' house and my grandmother's house had been burnt.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what was the time of day?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember it was at around 7.30 p.m. There was still fairly good visibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On your way to Bratunac, what other villages did you drive through; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We drove through Donja Kolonija, Kostanovice, Neskovici, Biljaca, Prisoj, Bjelovac, Zaluzje, Voljavice, Pobrdje, and then we got to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether anyone joined you at Pobrdje?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were joined by another soldier who was called Sale.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All those villages that you were driven through, it was in July 1992, right?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were all those villages under the control of the Serb army in June, that is to say the time when you were there, in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were under the control of the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what can you conclude that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Because on our way to Bratunac we could see many of their soldiers and they moved around freely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you move around freely in that car on your way to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you drove through those villages, do you remember seeing anything at Neskovici or not?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw a huge group of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember passing through Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. When we got to Bjelovac, there was a crossroads there going from Bratunac in the direction of Loznicka Rijeka, and Sase, and we stopped at the crossroads to let a column of APCs and tanks drive in the direction of Loznicka Rijeka. So they were going in the direction of Bratunac basically.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the same direction as Sikiric?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened to you next?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: When we got to Bratunac, those three soldiers took us to an abandoned Muslim house. I realised then that there was no cleaning job involved at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: We were taken into that house and we were raped and abused and beaten throughout the night, and I myself had a gun pointed at my head all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why you in particular?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Because I was screaming too much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How old were you at the time?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I was 15.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened to you on the next day?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It went on throughout that night and on the following morning they went somewhere and they left a guard there who was standing guard there, up until the evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened that evening?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Around 11.00 p.m., a group of soldiers came in. Among them was Novak Stjepanovic, aka Krke, and he appeared to be their leader.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you recognise anyone else from the group?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I recognised Sasa Cvetkovic and a neighbour by the name of Spasoje. Krsto Rankic as well. And he was from Bjelovac. And Krle from Zaluzje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. How did you know Krsto Rankic? Did he work somewhere?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: He used to work as a mine expert at the Sase mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And your father, where did he used to work?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: He used to work with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did those people do to you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: That evening, we were put in the cars again so we were taken out of the house, put in some other vehicles and we had to sit in their laps, and they took us around Bratunac and we ended up in a different house that was used at the time by Novak Stjepanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened to you that evening?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: We were raped again there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who raped you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Sasa Cvetkovic, Krsto Rankic, a person from Zaluzje who was called Krle, and a Milan from Sabac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would kindly ask the usher to put a list in front of the witness. It is an exhibit, D83, salaries for June of 1992. The number on the document is 01335404. And it is a list of the Territorial Defence of Bjelovac for June.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have tissues for the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Shall we have a short break, Madam Vidovic? Or Mrs. Karic -- Mrs. Karic, do you want a short break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will have the break now. We will have a 25-minute break. Thank you. We were supposed to have a break in 25 minutes in any case. So we'll have it now. Thank you. And if possible, let's try and get through this as quickly as you can, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Karic, I hope we can continue.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will not have many questions for you pertaining to these sensitive topics but just a few. Concerning those other girls, do you remember how old they were?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: They were between 15 and 18.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When we departed for the break, I was asking the usher to put D83 in front of the witness. I don't know whether you have a list of TO Bjelovac before you.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No, I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please ask the usher to put D83 in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do have D83.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My apologies then. Please go to the second page. This should be TO Bjelovac there. Did you find that? The first page says salaries for June of 1992. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It says, "People who were paid for official troop trip and pay."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please turn to the next page then. Do you see where it says TO Bjelovac at the top?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at number 571, Krsto Rankic, R?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the person that you said raped you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell the Chamber how old was that person at the time?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but he was in his middle age.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were describing us the events of that day. Were you later returned to the camp?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the rapings and during the night, in the morning they returned us to Sase, to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to talk with Mr. Miroljub Todorovic about the things that had happened to you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you tell him what happened?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We did. And he immediately called the entrance, the ramp, and he forbade them to let Krke within the mine perimeter.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You heard that yourself?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you nevertheless keep seeing Krke within the perimeter?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, tomorrow, the next day.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague just told me that something should be corrected in line 12 -- no, line 6, page 70. I will repeat the question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you tell him what happened and what did he do? You said that he made a phone call. Who did he call?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: He called the ramp that was located at the entrance to Donja Sase, and he said that Novak Stjepanovic, Krke, shouldn't be allowed inside the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say the ramp, you mean the place where the Serbs assembled? You mentioned that at the beginning of your testimony. Is that the thing?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you witness that conversation?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. We didn't know with whom he was speaking but we heard what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from what you have described, and what happened to you, I wanted to ask you whether there were some other rapes of other girls who remained behind in the camp after the large group departed.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that seldom or often?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It happened often.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I won't ask you about that anymore, but please tell the Chamber whether there was a person who particularly took part in those rapings, who did it the most?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was Ranko -- Petko Rankic, called Pero.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I would ask if we could have a period, a date? Are we still in June?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would imagine so. I mean, I don't think we have left that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: We haven't had a date in a while. I'm just seeking clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you could confirm this, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness was talking about the two weeks she spent in the camp starting from the end of May. She said she came there on the 27th and spent two weeks there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. And all this happened around the 5th or the 6th of July of 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, June.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said June?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: June. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness said June, and the transcript stated that it was July. I wanted to ask you the following: When did you leave the Sase mine?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Around the 11th of June of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: While you were still at the camp, were there -- was there any fighting?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was fighting on the very day we were transferred to Bratunac. In front of the building, there were numerous Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, Ms. Karic. You said that happened when we were transferred to Bratunac. And then you said in front of the building, many people assembled. Just to have it clear in the transcript. When you mentioned a -- or the building, are you still talking about the period of time when you were in Sase or are you mentioning a building in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: That's the administrative building in Gradina, in Sase.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You started telling us about some people who assembled there. What was taking place?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: They assembled, they started shooting around the building. They started calling us names. They kept saying "balija," and they wanted to kill us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who helped you then not to get killed?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was Miroljub Todorovic. He helped us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to Miroljub Todorovic, I wanted to ask you something about him. In your knowledge, did he personally partake in the mistreatment and rapings of the girls?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No. He didn't participate in the mistreatment and the rapes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to put another Defence exhibit before the Witness, P90. It is a book, the title of which is, "Srebrenica as a Witness and a Prosecutor." Or, "Srebrenica Testifies and Accuses." The page number is 0291976, which is page 30 in the English language.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the ERN number of the document in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to read out a passage to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you could please follow: "According to reliable sources".

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in English. Your Honour, to correct the number, 00816700.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: My apologies, but I don't have that page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We are talking about the English version, but you should have before you page 59 in Bosnian, and the ERN number should be 02919276. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will quote: "According to reliable sources, most of the detainees were killed and buried in the sludge deposit of the mine in Sase. A large number of the detained girls and women were raped. The ring leaders were Novak Stjepanovic, aka Krke, from the hamlet of Jaruge near Kostanovice and Lieutenant Miroljub Todorovic, who was the battery commander in Sase, as an outpost of the command in Bratunac." Ms. Karic, I have a couple of questions for you regarding this. In your assessment, was Miroljub Todorovic familiar with what was taking place there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in your assessment, did he personally participate and was he one of the ringleaders in the rapes and abuses?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the information that the author had, is it correct or not?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was actually the ringleader in the rapes?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Ringleader was Novak Stjepanovic, Krke, and Petko Rankic, aka Pero.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are throws local Serbs?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Richardson.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: If I may, with respect to the portion that was just read out to the witness, now, there is a mention of Todorovic's name. However, there is no indication that he was -- that he had taken part in the rapes. No indication from the book, that is. So to pose a question to the witness as such is misleading. They did mention that Krke was involved but based on the English version that I'm reading there is no indication that the commander was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But, Ms. Richardson, I disagree completely with you. If you read the previous sentence, because this is not a sentence that can be taken off apart from the rest. The sentence immediately preceding the one that has been read out to the witness is the following: "A large number of the detained girls and women were raped." Then immediately after, you have the ringleaders were Novak Stjepanovic, also known as Krke, from the hamlet of wherever, and Lieutenant Todorovic one of the first JNA ... So if one reads the two sentences together, what's the conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I have another question pertaining to this. The content of this passage that I read out to you, according to you, it's incorrect, is it not?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did someone transfer you to Bratunac on the 11th of June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, Miroljub Todorovic did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember what he told you during or prior to the transport? If you can remember. Just make a pause before you answer, please.

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: He said, "You have to go to Bratunac. You shouldn't stay here because of your Serb neighbours."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you came to Bratunac, where were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: First to the military police, and then to the Bratunac stadium in a restaurant that was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell the Chamber who took you to that restaurant, to that catering facility?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Miroljub Todorovic did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was he accompanied by anyone or was he alone?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: There was another soldier in the escort.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that person a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That place where you were taken to, can you remember what its interior looked like?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Whether we entered the room, it was full of blood. The tiles were splashed with blood. There were some white sheets there as well with bloodstains. There were things that -- thrown around the room.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing anything specific in that room, something that you recall?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember a blanket that belonged to Omic, Salcin, and there were two paintings or photographs by Mirzet.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness wasn't clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ramic Mirzet, is that the one plan who was taken from Likari the same day as you?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since it is unclear in the transcript, I wanted to ask the question again. It is stated here that you saw

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since it is unclear in the transcript, I wanted to ask the question again. It is stated here that you saw two paintings or photographs. What is it that you saw?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: I saw photographs of Mirzet Garaljevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will not ask a lot of questions about that period, as it is very disturbing for you. But I just wanted to ask you the following: Did Todorovic appear there at a certain moment?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. He appeared there on that very day. He came with a military truck and he took us to another abandoned Muslim house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So what happened with you who were there with the people that he brought to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: We spent a few days in that house. We were told not to turn the lights on and not to talk and not to look out of the window.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. In the end, did Mr. Todorovic help you in some way?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The day that we were brought to the house, he took the Omic family, Gordana and her son Damir and her daughter Vesna, he took them to Serbia, close to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he help you as well to them Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps to make things shorter, if I may be allowed to put a leading question, because some of the issues pertain to Serbia proper and is not directly linked to the indictment. I don't know if the Prosecution objects.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Richardson. Please go ahead, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were taken to Loznica, were you not?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you use your own name there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No. When we came there, we had to change our names.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Loznica?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: About a month and a half. More or less until mid-August.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And did you meet your husband there?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any point manage to go back to Bosnia and Herzegovina with your husband?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: It was in the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to put a couple of different questions to you. You testified today about what happened to you in May and in June 1992. And July 1992. Up until the point when you were transferred to Serbia. Where were your parents during that time?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: My parents were in the forests, the forest called Bare, and they stayed there up until mid-August, and then they somehow managed to get to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did your parents tell you whether they knew anything about those large numbers of Muslim people who stayed behind in the woods?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. They told me that masses of people stayed back in the woods and many of those people were completely exhausted, they were sick, they were going hungry, and some of them were actually going crazy in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did they mention anyone in particular who lost his mind?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. The mother of Mujic, Kiram lost her mind at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is she the only person to whom it had happened from your area or were there any others?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were many others, and many people actually died in those woods.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this respect, I'd like to put another question to you. Do you know anything -- have you heard anything from your parents as to how long those people stayed in the woods?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes. After they managed to get to Srebrenica, many other people actually stayed behind in the woods, and they stayed there until the end of that autumn, and many of those were later captured and killed when they tried to get back to their villages to look for food, and on those occasions they were either killed or captured.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Karic. Now I'd like to ask you something else. You told us today about the Serbs that you saw at the command post in Sase, and you also told us about other Serbs that you saw in the area that you were driven around in that vehicle, et cetera. On the basis of your experience and on the basis of what you heard from other Muslims about what went on in May and June 1992, can you now answer the following question? Were the Serbs that you saw them peace-loving individuals who were just sitting in their villages and keeping a watch on their property in the months of May and June 1992 in the area that you've described to us, Sase, Neskovici, Kostanovice, Bjelovac and Suha?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No, these were not village guards. It was an army with lots of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And was that a peaceful army or were they doing something else?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: No. They were killing, looting, raping, setting houses alight, and they perpetrated a great many crimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Karic, you made several statements in relation to everything that had happened to you and that had happened to other people, and events that you yourself had witnessed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether anyone ever has been held accountable for those killings and murders and rapes that you told us about?

utterances.speaker: EDINA KARIC
utterances.text: Nobody was -- has been held accountable for those acts, ever.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic. Are you going to start with your cross-examination now?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, tomorrow. Although, I can begin, if I can have a short break today. But it's my understanding that even if we do, I don't think the Defence is ready to start with their next witness tomorrow in any event, so I would appreciate starting tomorrow if we are not short on time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How much time do you think you will require tomorrow?.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Tomorrow, Your Honour, no more than an hour, hour and a half, tops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then we can give the witness a rest. I think that ought to be preferred rather than start again, if you agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. One small question before we send you to the hotel, Ms. Karic. This book by Sejo Omeragic that we saw before, there is a name of Enes Karic. Is he related to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, he isn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know him? Do you know who he is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So for today we are going to stop here. We will give you a well-deserved rest. Tomorrow we will continue at 9.00 in the morning, I think here, as well in this same courtroom. In the meantime, try to relax. You will have a short cross-examination tomorrow, and then you will be able to go back home and our staff will be making all the arrangements for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And good afternoon to everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of September, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.02 p.m.,
